label: Characteristic equation
subgoals: Write a y'' + b y' + c y = 0
Try y = e^{rx} to get a r^2 + b r + c = 0

slice.rule: For $a y'' + b y' + c y = 0$ with constant coefficients, try $y = e^{rx}$: it works exactly when $r$ solves the characteristic equation $a r^2 + b r + c = 0$. Two independent solutions span every solution.
slice.note: This is the linear homogeneous case ($Q(x) = 0$), not the first-order 'homogeneous' $y/x$ substitution; the word is used for both.

label: Three cases for the roots
subgoals: Distinct real roots: y = C1 e^{r1 x} + C2 e^{r2 x}
Repeated root: y = (C1 + C2 x) e^{rx}
Complex roots p ± qi: y = e^{px}(C1 cos qx + C2 sin qx)

slice.rule: The general solution depends on the discriminant $b^2 - 4ac$. Distinct real roots $r_1, r_2$: $y = C_1 e^{r_1 x} + C_2 e^{r_2 x}$. A repeated root $r$: $y = (C_1 + C_2 x)e^{rx}$. Complex roots $p \pm qi$: $y = e^{px}(C_1 \cos qx + C_2 \sin qx)$.

label: Initial value problems
subgoals: Use y(x0) and y'(x0) to find C1 and C2

slice.rule: Two initial conditions, $y(x_0)$ and $y'(x_0)$, fix the two constants: substitute into the general solution and its derivative and solve the pair of linear equations.
